clue.text: Retainer stupid to take such an interest in land

parts.note: a retainer is a fee paid in advance to secure someone's services
simple can mean foolish or slow-witted

explanation.surface: A dim-witted retainer is told to acquire a stake in some property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' is a link. FEE SIMPLE is the legal term for outright ownership of land.
explanation.definitionFit: In property law this is absolute freehold ownership, the fullest estate a person can hold in real property.

clue.text: Other birds head off these ones

definitions.text: Other birds head off these ones

parts.words: Other birds head off these ones
parts.note: take the first letter from these birds and different birds remain, the nocturnal hooting kind

explanation.surface: One flock of birds chases away another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' looks like heading birds off; it means removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry birds such as hens; beheaded, the name leaves the night-hunting birds of prey.

clue.text: Malevolent spirit of noble reported to monarch

indicators.note: reported indicates the word for the nobleman is spoken, so only its sound counts

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: An evil ghost belonging to an aristocrat is reported to the sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'to' are links. The Erl-King is the elf king of German legend in Goethe's ballad, set by Schubert.
explanation.definitionFit: In German folklore this goblin king lures children to their death, as in Goethe's ballad.

clue.text: Fashionable bouquet sent up, thanks to lover

parts.note: in means in fashion

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means read from bottom to top, so the scent word is written backwards

parts.note: a bouquet is the aroma of a wine
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A trendy bunch of flowers is dispatched, courtesy of a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns AROMA into AMORA. 'bouquet' suggests flowers but means a wine's scent; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is loved, a sweetheart or mistress, from the Italian.

clue.text: Utter superiority of prior to cardinal?

parts.note: pre- means before
His Eminence is the style of a Roman Catholic cardinal

explanation.surface: A monastery prior defers completely to a cardinal's higher rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prior' reads as a monk but is part of 'prior to', before; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This means outstanding excellence or rank above all others, total distinction.

clue.text: Leaders of mass movement met in German town

wordplay.reading: M M M: the leaders are the letter M, plural Ms

parts.note: each of the three words begins with the letter M, so the leaders are Ms, spelt out as the letter's name in the plural

explanation.surface: The heads of a mass movement gathered in a town in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The three leaders are all M; the name of the letter M is 'em', so several are 'ems'. 'in' is a link. Bad Ems is a German spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad Ems is a spa in Rhineland-Palatinate, known simply by this short name.

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: the three blind mice lose their eye: the closing E is blotted out, as a blind blots out a window

parts.note: mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: A firm deals in sightless rodents, which sounds like a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blind' cuts the final E from MICE to leave MIC, set after CO; the nursery-rhyme three blind mice prompt the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comic is amusing and makes people laugh, the adjective sense matching the clue word.

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters inside the next word

explanation.surface: A young woman forms part of a formal statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Clara is a girl's first name, and a Miss is an unmarried woman or girl.

definitions.meaning: a fortified wine from Portugal's Atlantic island
describes a type of plain sponge cake

explanation.surface: Someone drinks heavily, soaking it up like a sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: Madeira cake is a plain British sponge cake, once served with a glass of the fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from the Atlantic island, and the plain sponge cake named for being eaten with it.

parts.note: a cross is the mark a voter puts on a ballot paper
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A voter is seen as introspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. 'inward looking' usually means introspective; here it is literal, eyes turned towards the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a squint in which both eyes turn towards the nose, so they literally gaze inwards.

clue.text: Good time went very quickly? Just the reverse

indicators.note: the clue tells the solver to turn the whole string round, so the word era plus flew is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time
flew means sped along

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that a good time passed in a flash, then corrects that to the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' turns ERAFLEW round to give the answer. 'Good' is a noun here: the common good, well-being.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare is well-being or benefit, as in acting for someone's good or advantage.

clue.text: Take up position as booth closed

parts.note: a stand is a stall or booth at a fair or exhibition
to as an adverb means shut, as in pulling a door to

explanation.surface: Someone stations themselves by a booth that has shut for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. Soldiers ordered to stand to take their posts ready for attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A military order: troops told this move to their action stations, ready for any attack.

indicators.note: the hyphen joins sounding to crafty, so only the spoken form of the cunning word is used

parts.note: sly means cunning or crafty
a go is a turn or move in a game

explanation.surface: A cunning-seeming manoeuvre is made on behalf of some county.
explanation.walkthrough: SLY GO said aloud gives the Irish county; 'for' is a link. Sligo is a county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is one of the counties of Ireland, in Connacht on the Atlantic coast.

indicators.note: dreadful suggests a mess, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Tradesmen suffer a terrible piece of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges MISCHANCE; the possessive 's on workers is a link ('have').
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanics are trained manual tradesmen who repair and maintain engines and machinery.

clue.text: Report accusation of price increase for consumer

parts.note: to cover a story is to report on it
a charge is a formal accusation

explanation.surface: A news report about a claim that consumers are paying higher prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. A cover charge is added to a restaurant bill per diner.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed extra sum added to a bill in a restaurant or nightclub for each customer.

definitions.meaning: the on side of a cricket field
a stage of a trip or relay

explanation.surface: Something sits on one stretch of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg is the cricket name for the on side, and also one stage of a longer trip or race.

definitions.meaning: the main town of an English county
the Tudor queen's favourite held the earldom of this name

explanation.surface: A county town has links with clue 20.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester is the county town of Leicestershire in the English Midlands; Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was Queen Elizabeth I's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The administrative centre of a Midlands shire, and the earldom of Elizabeth I's favourite Robert Dudley.

clue.text: Point arrives, perhaps, in any day of celebration

indicators.note: the point and the jumbled letters are placed within the word any

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters given are only one possible arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A compass point turns up on some date of festivities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ARRIVES into IVERSAR; with N in front this goes between AN and Y of ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: An anniversary is the yearly date marking a past event, kept as an occasion for festivities.

parts.note: red is a colour
IV is four in Roman numerals, and fours gives it twice
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Someone wearing coloured plus fours in America has been brought back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plus fours' are baggy golfing trousers; 'plus' is really a link. Redivivus is Latin for come back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin word used in English after a noun for someone or something revived or reborn.

parts.note: ill means badly, as in ill-treated
mannered means artificial or affected in style

explanation.surface: A Saxon in Kipling's verse is seen as sick and pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kipling's poem 'Norman and Saxon' the dying Norman baron warns his son that the Saxon's manners are rough and unpolished.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's Saxon is portrayed as blunt and lacking politeness, which is to say rude in behaviour.

clue.text: Dallies with love in transatlantic volumes

indicators.note: in tells us the love letter goes inside the volumes

parts.note: liters is the American spelling of litres, units of volume
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone lingers with a sweetheart among American books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volumes' looks like books; it means measures of capacity, spelt the US way. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly or hang about, so the verb matches dallies.

definitions.meaning: a son of Jacob who gave his name to an Israelite tribe
a minced oath, short for 'by God!'

explanation.surface: A tribal warrior's exclamation of shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Gad was a son of Jacob, founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel; 'Gad!' is an old mild oath. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the tribe descended from Jacob's son of that name, and a dated euphemistic oath for God.

clue.text: Part of house full of rogues, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a raised balcony area in a theatre or legislative chamber
the police photo collection called a rogues' display

explanation.surface: A wing of a house is crammed with villains.
explanation.walkthrough: A rogues' gallery is a police collection of photos of criminals; the theatre's gallery is its top tier, the 'gods'.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper seating level of a theatre or parliament, and the room of portraits in the rogues' collection.

parts.note: the first queen of a two-monarch line, whose name also begins the regnal title of the second, the present one numbered two

explanation.surface: The earlier of a duo sets off at two o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: England has had two queens of this name, I and II; the first is the 16th-century Tudor queen linked to Leicester at 14 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor monarch who was first of her name, followed centuries later by a second queen so called.

parts.note: an empty space or vacuum, a situation with nothing at its heart, is a void

explanation.surface: Get out of a loveless state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' suggests cruelty but means empty at the centre; 'say' marks a loose example.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to keep clear of it or evade it, as escape can mean.

clue.text: Inconclusive steps taken to get servant

indicators.note: without a conclusion, so the final letter of the word for the dance steps is cut off

parts.note: the valeta is an old-time ballroom dance, a sequence of steps

explanation.surface: Half-hearted dance moves are made to land a manservant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inconclusive' drops the last A of VALETA, a waltz-style sequence dance; 'taken to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A valet is a gentleman's personal manservant who looks after his clothes.

definitions.meaning: alludes to the saying that commerce follows the national banner

explanation.surface: Vehicles wait behind a flag-waver.
explanation.walkthrough: The old saying 'trade follows the flag' holds that commerce comes after colonial conquest.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce or dealing, which in the proverb comes after a nation's banner has been planted.

clue.text: Artist's connection with Merchant of Venice

parts.note: a tie is a link or bond
Marco Polo was a Venetian merchant and traveller

explanation.surface: A painter is linked to Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merchant of Venice' suggests Shakespeare's play but means Marco Polo. The 's is 'is'; 'with' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an 18th-century Venetian painter famed for ceiling frescoes.

explanation.surface: Someone halted and went elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Switched off or cancelled, and also absent or departed, as in a day out of the office.

parts.note: read Nice as the French resort city, not the adjective, and think of the coastline around it

explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised at the start, 'Nice' hides the city on the Côte d'Azur.
explanation.definitionFit: The French coast on the Mediterranean, where Nice lies, is known by this Italian-derived name.

indicators.note: the word soundly tells us the built word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: raised means put up or erected, as a building

explanation.surface: Something knocked down, which had been well constructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's' is a link. RASED (more often razed) means levelled to the ground, the opposite of the word it sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: To rase is to level a building to the ground, an older spelling of the verb meaning to tear down.

parts.note: free can mean too familiar, as in free with one's hands
a style is a title or name, as in being styled 'Sir'

explanation.surface: A well-known name competes in a race at the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimming race in which competitors may use any stroke, in practice the front crawl.
